stage1.impression: A warm, well-composed night view down a long narrow bar with real depth and pools of light, but it still reads as a CG render: thick milky haze veils the whole back bar, the floor stains look like a stamped decal, five identical stools and five identical lamps march down the room, and the right-hand screens glow like flat poster lightboxes. The EARF speakers are not the hero: the altar pair are two small pale boxes 15 m away, the back-bar speaker is washed to grey behind the haze, and the only strong colour in the frame is the orange of the beams and timber, not the product. A magazine would see a handsome but generic 'moody bar' render, not yet a specific place.

blocking_9: The haze must stop veiling the back bar: the bar-pair speaker [110,300,175,420] needs its woofer and cabinet dark again (lum_p5 below 45, now 106)
The speakers must be read at a glance as tinted acrylic horns, not pale boxes: the altar pair need contrast against a darker altar wall and visible edge glow through the smoked acrylic
The room surfaces must read neutral: ceiling beams and timber are saturated orange (ceiling RGB median 64/31/10, b nearly zero), so the room, not the product, carries the colour
The floor concrete must read as polished board-formed/troweled concrete at 1:1, not a repeating blotch decal
Furniture repetition must be broken (chairs turned, one pulled out, coats, glasses at different states) so the room looks lived in
The framed screens on the right must not read as flat lightboxes: their brightness must sit below the bar top

defects.what: Back-bar speaker washed out by haze and pendant spill: lum_median 154, lum_p5 106; woofer reads grey, cabinet invisible
Record wall and back bar milky and low-contrast; shelving reads as pale pink boards, no record spines or highlights
Zinc counter top lum_median 150, reads as a flat bright grey plane with no patina or reflection detail
Altar speakers tiny (about 45 px wide) and read as white boxes with a big woofer; no tint, no acrylic edge glow; spot cones visible as hard haze shafts
Floor stains are uniform soft blotches repeated across the floor, read as a decal/texture, not concrete; no polish reflections of the lamps
Ceiling beams saturated orange (RGB median 64/31/10, delta E 10.6 against a neutral warm fir #5A4030); no checks or nail holes at 1:1
Large screen is a flat even glow (lum_median 107) with a soft blob image; reads as a lightbox poster, not a frosted acrylic screen
Second screen same flat glow and blurry blob image
Five identical stools at identical angles and five identical Orb lamps in a row: repeated copies of one model
Banquette crushes toward black (lum_median 21) with no leather sheen or detail
Hard, straight haze shafts from the pendants read as a render effect

changes.problem: Haze veils the whole back of the room and lifts every black there, so the back-bar speaker and record wall go milky and the frame reads as CG fog.

evidence.measured: lum_median 153.6, lum_p5 106.2, lum_range 126: no true dark anywhere in the speaker

change.setting: haze in the room's air (density per metre)

changes.expected: Back bar regains its darks; the bar speaker's woofer and cabinet edge become legible; the pendant shafts soften to a faint atmosphere.

changes.problem: The grade turns the fir and stain into saturated orange, so the room carries colour that should belong only to the product.

evidence.measured: RGB median 64/31/10, delta E 10.6 against neutral warm fir #5A4030

changes.expected: Timber and concrete settle to warm neutrals (blue channel no longer near zero); smoked acrylic and the zinc separate from the wood.

changes.problem: The altar pair, the frame's hero, are small pale boxes that do not out-shine their surroundings or show their tinted acrylic.

evidence.measured: lum_median 46 (left), 36.6 at [655,330,700,435]; same level as the surrounding back zone (34.3 at [420,280,830,500])

change.to: 220 W, cone 18 deg, aimed at the cabinets' upper edge so light passes through the acrylic; drop the room's back wall exposure by keeping the Domes' downlights as in c4

changes.expected: The two speakers become the brightest, most defined objects at the far end, with a tight falloff around them and a dark altar wall behind.

changes.problem: The zinc counter and the back bar are the brightest large surfaces, pulling the eye to the left foreground instead of the altar.
changes.expected: Tighter pools on the bar with darker zinc between them; the counter shows patina and reflections of the glasses rather than a flat grey plane.

changes.problem: The frosted screens on the right glow as flat bright lightboxes and compete with the speakers.

evidence.measured: lum_median 106.7, p5 31, p95 126: an even flat panel brighter than the floor and altar

changes.expected: The screens fall to a soft glow below the bar top, reading as frosted acrylic in a dim room.

changes.problem: The floor reads as a stamped blotch texture with no polish; real concrete would show trowel marks and soft reflections of the Orbs and table bases.

evidence.measured: lum p5 8.3, p95 158.7 from blotches alone; no specular reflections of the Orbs visible

change.setting: the floor's polish (roughness) and stain contrast
change.to: roughness about 0.35 with a low-contrast stain at half the current strength

changes.expected: Soft elongated reflections of the Orbs and the bar's under-light on the floor; stains become faint and irregular.

changes.problem: Identical stools and Orb lamps at identical angles repeat down the room and read as copies of one model, not a lived-in bar.

evidence.measured: five chairs and five Orbs at the same rotation and spacing

change.from: all chairs square to tables, one coat in the frame
change.to: rotate each chair 5 to 25 deg differently, pull one out, add a coat over the nearest chair, a record sleeve and two half-full glasses on the near tables, a menu on the bar

changes.expected: The foreground reads as a room paused mid-evening; repetition breaks.

changes.problem: The banquette on the right crushes toward black with no leather sheen, leaving a dead right-hand third.
changes.expected: Each Orb throws a small pool onto its table and the banquette's leather catches a soft edge sheen.

out_of_scope.request: Make the speakers larger in the frame, or tint them a saturated colour so they read as the one colour
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's colour (Smoke configuration) and the room layout are fixed; only camera and light may change. A tighter lens or a camera further in would help but changes the hero framing the card fixes as 'from the door'.

out_of_scope.request: Replace the repeated stool model with varied seating
out_of_scope.why: The seats are part of the room's design as proposed.

out_of_scope.request: Change the images shown on the screens to something sharper
out_of_scope.why: The screens and what they show are fixed by the card.
